subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Bottom Line Up Front
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bottom Line Up Front.

hook.text: The US military teaches BLUF: bottom line up front. Give the conclusion first, then the supporting evidence.

buildup.text: Busy leaders lose patience with long buildups. By the time you reach the point, they have mentally moved on.

discovery.text: BLUF respects your boss's time and attention. Lead with the answer and let them ask for detail if they need it.

twist.text: BLUF feels risky because you lose the narrative arc. But executives consume information differently than peers.

climax.text: Structure every update as: recommendation, key evidence, risk, and next step. All in four sentences or fewer.

punchline.text: Lead with the answer. Let them ask for more.

quiz.question: What does BLUF stand for and why does it work with leaders?
options: Bottom Line Under Focus — it hides risks until later
Bottom Line Up Front — it respects busy leaders' time
Best Logic Under Fire — it works in crises only
